sources.entry: Postiz ⚠ - Schedule posts, track the performance of your content, and manage all your social media accounts in one place (Alternative to Buffer, Hootsuite, Sprout Social). (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Postiz is an open-source, self-hostable social media management platform for scheduling, automating, and analyzing posts across multiple social accounts.
summary.what_it_does: Postiz lets you schedule social media posts across multiple channels, with a calendar view, cross-posting, repeated posts, comments, and delays. It includes analytics for tracking content performance, though analytics require your own platform app credentials with analytics scopes in the self-hosted edition. Team features let members collaborate, comment, and schedule posts, and exchange or buy posts. It offers a public API and integration paths for automation tools such as N8N, Make.com, and Zapier, plus AI features (copilot, images, videos, and a smart agent) that the self-hosted version runs on your own provider API keys. The project is a pnpm monorepo built with NextJS, NestJS, Prisma (defaulting to PostgreSQL), Temporal, and Resend for email notifications.
use_cases: Schedule posts to multiple social media accounts
Track performance of social media content
Manage team collaboration on social posts
Automate posting via API or N8N/Make.com workflows
how_to_run: Follow the Quick Start Guide linked in the README
Deploy with Docker, Coolify, Railway, or on any VPS (per README)
notable: Open-source self-hosted edition alongside a managed Postiz Cloud service with the same core features
Public API with a NodeJS SDK, N8N custom node, and Make.com integration
Agentic surfaces including MCP, CLI, and connectors for AI assistants
Team collaboration with comments, shared post exchange, and invitations
Built on a pnpm monorepo with NextJS frontend and NestJS backend
caveats: Self-hosting requires you to configure Postgres, Redis, storage, and env vars, and to create your own developer apps on each social platform, which can take weeks for approval (Meta, YouTube, TikTok named)
Analytics and AI features in the self-hosted edition require your own app credentials and provider API keys
The README says self-hosted deployment can be hard at times and suggests using an LLM to help deploy it
